prompt.context: We are consulting for a UK consumer bank in 2010. The client offers products including credit cards, debit cards, insurance, mutual funds, checking accounts, and mortgages. Its mutual fund business, called Mutual Co., has experienced a decline in profitability over the past 5 years. It sells to new accounts through both its direct channel of in-house tele-sales representatives and indirectly cross-selling its mutual fund products through its insurance business. Mutual Co. earns revenue by charging an annual fixed percentage management fee times each account balance. Mutual Co.'s new CEO has hired McKinsey to identify why profitability has declined within the unit and to recommend specific actions to improve it.
prompt.question: Why has Mutual Co.'s profitability declined over the past 5 years, and what specific actions can be taken to improve it?

clarifying_info.q: Has the number of accounts decreased?
clarifying_info.a: The number of accounts has not decreased.

clarifying_info.q: Is this decline unique to our client?
clarifying_info.a: Competitors have experienced a similar decline in profitability.

clarifying_info.q: What is the management fee rate?
clarifying_info.a: Management fees are 0.5% of the account balance.

clarifying_info.q: How many accounts does Mutual Co. have?
What is the current average account balance?
clarifying_info.a: The average account balance is currently $5,000.

clarifying_info.q: What are the variable costs per account?
clarifying_info.a: The costs of managing each account are $20 (these are the variable costs).

clarifying_info.q: What are the total fixed costs?
clarifying_info.a: All other costs are $35M in total (these are the fixed costs).

framework: Revenue analysis: Revenue = management fee % x total assets under management. Total AUM = number of accounts x average account balance. Investigate whether fee % has changed or whether total AUM has changed.
Cost analysis: Break into fixed costs (compliance, SG&A, rent, IT) and variable costs (exchange fees, paperwork, customer service costs per transaction/call).

Narrow the driver: With costs flat and account count flat, the root cause must be a decline in average account balance per account, likely driven by the 2007-2008 financial crisis depressing equity prices.

questions.prompt: Identify the root cause of the profitability decline using a MECE structure.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a revenue/cost or internal/external tree. Revenue = fee % x AUM; AUM = accounts x avg balance. With variable costs unchanged, fixed costs unchanged, and account count unchanged, the only remaining driver is a decline in average account balance — attributable to the post-2008 fall in equity prices affecting UK markets similarly to US markets.

questions.prompt: What average account balance would Mutual Co. need to achieve a 10% profit margin?
questions.guidance: Candidate should: (1) compute total cost per account = fixed cost per account + variable cost per account; (2) gross up to required revenue per account for a 10% margin; (3) divide by the fee rate to get required balance. A 10% profit margin means revenue = cost / (1 - 0.10), i.e., revenue = cost x (1/0.9) or equivalently revenue = cost x 1.111.

math.setup: Fixed costs per account = $35M / 1,000,000 = $35. Variable cost per account = $20. Total cost per account = $55. Required revenue per account for 10% margin = $55 / 0.90 = $61.11. Required avg balance = $61.11 / 0.005.
math.answer: The average account balance must be approximately $12,200 to achieve a 10% profit margin.

questions.prompt: What specific actions can Mutual Co. take to increase profitability?
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate a MECE revenue/cost structure. Revenue levers: review and improve incentives for the parent company's indirect (insurance) sales force to cross-sell mutual fund products; run new promotions to attract deposits; benchmark the management fee % against industry average and consider raising it if demand is inelastic; expand geographically. Variable cost levers: shift from paper to electronic communications (current $20/account variable cost is high); use third-party mutual funds instead of in-house managed funds, which may be cheaper. Fixed cost levers: consolidate support functions (HR, IT, Finance) with the parent bank; consolidate office locations to reduce rent.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the possible reasons profitability has declined? Use a MECE structure.

categories.name: Revenue decline
ideas: Management fee percentage charged has been reduced
Average account balance has fallen due to market depreciation (post-2008 financial crisis)
Cross-sell conversion from insurance channel has weakened

categories.name: Cost increase — Variable
ideas: Higher paperwork or mailing costs per transaction
Increased customer service costs (more calls or longer call times)

categories.name: Cost increase — Fixed
ideas: Higher compliance costs from new financial regulation (e.g., Dodd-Frank analogs in UK)

recommendation: Mutual Co.'s profitability decline is primarily driven by a fall in average account balances caused by post-2008 equity market depreciation, which reduced AUM and therefore management fee revenue without a corresponding cost reduction.
To restore a 10% profit margin, average account balance must rise from $5,000 to approximately $12,200 — a 2.4x increase — requiring both revenue and cost actions.
risks: Raising management fees may cause customer attrition if competitors do not follow suit
Equity markets may remain depressed or decline further, limiting organic balance recovery
Cross-selling efficiency depends on incentive alignment with the insurance sales force, which may be slow to change
next_steps: Benchmark management fee rate against UK mutual fund industry peers
Design an incentive scheme for the insurance sales force to prioritize mutual fund cross-sells
Audit variable cost structure to reduce the $20/account variable cost (e.g., move to electronic statements)
Explore consolidation of support functions with the parent bank to reduce fixed costs
